title: How the Account Buys: Measuring the Monthly Purchase Base of a Commercial Credit Account
content:
For the supported limit of a Commercial Credit Account, **the monthly purchase base** is measured by how the account buys.

### Clause

The monthly purchase base is measured by how the account buys: for an account billed monthly consolidated whose latest statement, meaning the invoice totals posted on the latest invoice date, is at least one and a half times the twelve-month average month, it is that latest statement; for an account billed monthly consolidated whose latest statement is at least one and one fifth times the twelve-month average month but less than one and a half times it, it is the average of that latest statement and the twelve-month average month; otherwise it is the twelve-month average, and an account with no invoice has a monthly purchase base of nothing.

The twelve-month average month is the invoice totals posted on the account in the last twelve whole months divided by 12.

### Ladder

| Billing cycle | Latest statement against the twelve-month average month | Monthly purchase base |
|---|---|---|
| monthly consolidated | 150 percent or more | the latest statement |
| monthly consolidated | 120 percent or more, below 150 percent | the average of the latest statement and the twelve-month average month |
| monthly consolidated | below 120 percent | the twelve-month average month |
| per shipment | any | the twelve-month average month |
| no invoice on the account | — | nothing |

### Boundary cases (hypothetical, twelve-month average month 20000.00, consolidated billing)

- Latest statement 30000.00 (exactly one and a half times): base 30000.00.
- Latest statement 29999.99: base the average of 29999.99 and 20000.00, 24999.995 unrounded.
- Latest statement 24000.00 (exactly one and one fifth times): base 22000.00.
- Latest statement 23999.99: base 20000.00.
